title: Fylgja verdict 1
description: A domain verdict: what a compile, a package validation, a plan, a run (create, step, destroy) or a verification concluded, with every finding that led there. Anything malformed or refused at the door is a problem document (problem-1), never a verdict.
$comment: EXIT CODES, on the thin CLI only: ok -> 0; rejected, failed, nonconforming -> 1 (a negative verdict); unclean, diverged -> 3 (the twin is left dirty); a problem document or a transport failure -> 2. STATUS. ok: done as asked. rejected: refused on its merits before the runtime was touched (a compile, a package, admission). failed: failed after the runtime was touched, and cleanup completed. unclean: failed, and something remains (the run's findings name it). diverged: a step failed or was cancelled after touching the twin, and nothing was torn down. nonconforming: verify read every node and intent is not met. RULES. One stable dotted id per rule; the rule catalogue, written with the code that files the rules, is user documentation under docs/.

findings_version.description: The format's version; clients refuse any other.

operation.description: What reached the verdict; the CLI chooses its rendering by it.

status.description: The verdict; the CLI maps it to an exit code and the orchestrator branches on it.

twin.description: The twin the verdict is about; clients link to it.

run_id.description: The run the verdict ends; clients read its events by it.

blueprint_id.description: The blueprint compiled or run; clients and the orchestrator's report cite it.

bundle_id.description: The bundle built, run or verified against; clients and the report cite it.

deployment_id.description: The deployment planned or applied; clients cite it.

subject.description: What the verdict is about; only the ids that apply are present, and none for a package validation, which is about the package the request carried.

findings.description: Every finding, sorted by (severity, rule, object); clients render each, the orchestrator's report quotes them.

held.description: Assertions that held; the CLI and the report's verify cell show it.

failed.description: Assertions that failed, each also a finding; the CLI and the report show it.

skipped.description: Assertions not made (a disabled port, a synthesized link's neighbour), each an info finding; the CLI and the report show it.

counts.description: Verify's assertion counts, bursts included; present on verify and on a step whose wait verified.

outcome.description: Whether verify held within the budget; the step's status and the report read it.

budget_s.description: The wait's bound; the report states it.

after_s.description: Seconds from the push to the wait's end; the report states it.

wait.description: A step's wait for verify to hold; present on step only.

loss.description: Each probe's flow across the step, sorted by (probe, from); reported, never asserted. Present on step only, [] with no probes.

rule.description: A stable dotted rule id (e.g. probe.interface.cabled).
The rule; clients and tests match on it, never on message.

severity.description: error makes the verdict negative; clients colour and filter by it.

object.description: What the finding is about (n1, n1:ethernet-1/1, n1-loop, a JSON pointer); clients group by it.

message.description: One plain sentence of the fault's facts, never markup or a credential; clients print it.

probe.description: The probe's name; the report's loss column keys on it.

from.description: The host the flow ran from; the report shows each direction.

outcome.description: Whether counters were read; dropped when the step's target removed the probe. The report reads it.

sent.description: Packets sent; present when measured. The report shows it.

lost.description: Packets unanswered; present when measured. The report shows it.

longest_gap_s.description: The longest run of unanswered packets in seconds; present when measured. The report shows it.
